title: NNSA recurring qualified rate receives bounded algorithm and key-compromise recovery
summary: A declared compromise freezes and revokes the affected key, disables its algorithm, requires a distinct replacement key and algorithm, threshold authorization, witnessed checkpoint, trusted time, and independent historical re-verification while reconstructed state remains inactive. Denominator: One compromise-recovery schema, twenty-six adversarial cases, seven valid or preservation routes, nineteen explicit rejections, and zero actual compromise events, recovery actions, algorithm migrations, or reader activations.
